title: Version handshake protocol for preserved IO signatures
creator: Aisha Rahman
description:
Summary: Define and implement a compact 'handshake' manifest and runtime validation for newly onboarded model versions such that prompt shapes, response structure, and exposed parameter names are explicitly declared, automatically validated at rollout time, and published alongside the performance profile. This reduces downstream breakages when customers pin a version and safeguards Console routing and SDKs that depend on stable IO signatures.

Background: We frequently see subtle regressions when minor model variants change tokenization, parameter names (max_tokens -> max_output_tokens), or output structure (single field vs array). Existing onboarding artifacts capture compatibility informally (PR notes, evals) but there's no machine-readable contract that the router/console and SDKs can assert against during deploy. This ticket builds a lightweight manifest + verification flow and a runtime 'adapter' layer to handle safe aliases for deprecated parameter names.

Goals (non-exhaustive):
- Create a compact Version Handshake Manifest format (JSON schema) that records: accepted prompt formats (text, chat, structured JSON), canonical output shape(s) with examples, parameter names and aliases, default values, and published perf metrics (p50/p95 latency for 512/2048 tokens, tokens/s throughput).
- Add an onboarding verification step that runs the manifest against a golden prompt set and a regression harness (behavioral and perf checks).
- Surface mismatches as blocking errors for a pinned release and enable automated minor-alias adapters where safe.
- Publish manifest and performance profile to the model catalog endpoint so Console and SDKs can query compatibility before routing.

Non-goals: Full schema evolution language or stateful contract negotiation across different model families. We will focus on preserving the IO signature surface for pinned versions only.

Design notes:
- Manifest format will be intentionally small and versioned (e.g. handshake_v1). Fields: id, model_version, prompt_schema_type, canonical_output_example, parameter_map (canonical_name -> {type, required, aliases}), perf_snapshot (latency p50/p95 for typical seq lengths), checksum for golden prompts.
- Runtime enforcement will occur in two places: (1) onboarding pipeline: run golden prompts, compare outputs using tolerant diff (token-level similarity + structured field presence). (2) router/console at rollout: before enabling traffic, validate incoming request surface against parameter_map and reject mismatched calls unless adapter exists.
- Adapter behaviour: if a request uses a known alias, the runtime will map to canonical name and emit telemetry. If an ambiguous alias is used that maps to multiple canonical parameters, the request will be rejected and logged for manual remediation.
- Publishing: manifest served via model catalog API at /models/{model_id}/versions/{version}/handshake. SDKs will fetch manifest at startup or cache with TTL. Console shows deprecation/alias warnings when user config references aliases.

Acceptance criteria:
- A handshake_v1 schema is defined and checked into docs (Confluence + JSON Schema).
- Onboarding pipeline rejects versions where golden-prompt structural mismatches exceed thresholds (presence/absence of top-level fields).
- Runtime adapter implements parameter alias mapping with telemetry and a fail-open flag disabled by default for pinned releases.
- Model catalog exposes the manifest and perf snapshot for every onboarded pinned version.
- Unit and integration tests covering alias mapping, mismatch detection, and manifest publishing exist and run in CI.

Test plan:
- Create a control model package with deliberate alias changes and output-shape changes. Onboard it through the pipeline and validate that handshake check fails where expected.
- Add an alias mapping entry and ensure the adapter maps traffic correctly and emits telemetry.
- Perf snapshots: run perf harness for 512/2048 tokens and verify values are published to the catalog.
- End-to-end: perform a canary rollout (1% traffic) via Dedicated routing to validate runtime behavior in production-like environment, monitor Console for mismatch alerts.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: Spec + JSON Schema review (PM/Design/Infra).
- Week 2: Implement manifest writer and onboarding verifier in onboarding pipeline; add CI regression tests.
- Week 3: Implement runtime adapter and catalog publishing; integrate with Console to display manifest metadata.
- Week 4: Canary rollouts for a small set of internal models, collect telemetry, iterate. Full enable for pinned-version onboarding in release runtime-2.4.

Risks and mitigations:
- False positives on structural checks: mitigate by using tolerant diffs and allowing per-field optional flags in manifest.
- Increased onboarding friction: provide automated alias suggestions and a CLI tool to generate baseline manifest from example prompts/outputs.
- SDK cache staleness: include manifest TTL and a versioned etag header to force refresh on rollout.

Artifacts and links: Spec draft, eval harness, and related PRs are listed below.
acceptance_criteria:
1) handshake_v1 JSON Schema committed to docs and linked from onboarding pipeline.
2) Onboarding pipeline rejects a test model with missing top-level output fields by default.
3) Adapter maps single known aliases and emits telemetry; ambiguous aliases cause rejection.
4) Handshake manifest and perf snapshot appear in model catalog at /models/{id}/versions/{v}/handshake.
5) CI tests covering manifest validation and adapter behavior present and green.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for JSON Schema validation (positive + negative cases).
- Regression harness runs golden prompts and compares outputs using token-similarity threshold + structured-field checks.
- Integration test: simulate router receiving alias param and verify mapping + telemetry.
- Canary: deploy to staging Dedicated cluster and route 1% traffic for 24h and monitor for errors and perf regressions.
progress_notes: 2026-03-01: Ticket created by Aisha. Initial spec sketched; PM and infra pinged for review.
2026-03-03: Kickoff meeting with Priya Desai (PM) and Miguel Torres (Infra). Agreed on minimal manifest fields and performance snapshot targets.
2026-03-05: Prototype JSON Schema (handshake_v1) checked in to docs branch (link below). Onboarding verifier stub added to pipeline; failing tests identified due to tokenizer mismatch handling.
2026-03-09: Runtime adapter prototype implements alias mapping and basic telemetry. Internal test shows alias mapping works for single-alias case; ambiguous mapping left as reject.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on the JSON Schema and the tolerant-diff rules for structured outputs. Pay special attention to alias semantics: we should only allow one-to-one alias mappings automatically. Anything many-to-one should require manual remediation. Also confirm perf snapshot shape meets Console consumption needs.
